title: Quantum Computing : A New Frontier for Science and Society
abstract: This short report explores the (non exhaustive) current state of quantum technologies, their potential applications, and the challenges that must be addressed to harness their full potential. In particular we will focus on the quantum computer architecture and its ecosystem. Such architecture represents a complex, multi-layered system that integrates quantum and classical components to enable the execution of quantum algorithms. This manuscript is then organized as follows : first we will introduce the quantum processing unit, the lowest layer of a quantum computer. Then we will progress from the lowest to the higher layer of the system architectures : measurement, circuit control, error correction and mitigation system, the quantum compiler and finally the software stack, with particular emphasis on the interactions between these components
summary: This report surveys the current landscape of quantum technologies, analyzing the complex, multi-layered architecture required for practical quantum computation. It compares leading hardware platforms—such as trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and neutral atoms—while detailing critical challenges like decoherence and the necessity of robust Quantum Error Correction. The paper emphasizes that future progress relies on integrating these physical systems with advanced classical control electronics.
main_problem: Developing quantum technologies capable of solving problems intractable for classical computation, while managing inherent hardware limitations like decoherence.
main_result: The field is rapidly advancing across multiple platforms (superconducting, trapped ion, neutral atom), demonstrating progress towards fault-tolerant logical qubits and achieving early forms of quantum advantage in specific tasks.
method: The report reviews the entire technological stack, from physical qubit implementation to high-level software compilation, emphasizing error correction codes and hybrid classical-quantum control loops.
model_or_system: It compares several hardware modalities: superconducting circuits (transmons), trapped ions ($	ext{Yb}^+, 	ext{Ca}^+$), neutral atoms in optical lattices, photonic systems, and silicon spin qubits. The discussion heavily features quantum error correction codes like the surface code.
key_observables: Decoherence time, Gate Fidelity, Logical Error Rate, Quantum Volume, and qubit connectivity.
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperatures ($\sim 10-20 	ext{ mK}$), gate operation timescales ($\mu	ext{s}$ to ns), and physical overhead required for error correction.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the complex, multi-layered architecture (QPU $ightarrow$ Control $ightarrow$ Compiler $ightarrow$ Software) can be successfully integrated and scaled.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the layered architecture of a quantum computer stack, progressing from software down to the physical QPU layer.
paper_structure: The paper is structured as a comprehensive review, moving systematically from foundational concepts (superposition, entanglement) to hardware platforms (Superconducting, Trapped Ion, etc.), and culminating in advanced topics like Quantum Error Correction codes and system integration challenges.
why_interesting: It provides an excellent overview of the state-of-the-art across multiple quantum computing modalities, detailing the specific physical control mechanisms (lasers, microwaves) and error correction techniques relevant to open quantum systems research.
